Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Tejas Networks Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference 
Call hosted by Emkay Global Financial Services Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will 
be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star, then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is 
being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Aryan Tripathi, Emkay Global Financial Services 
Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Aryan Tripathi: 
Good evening, everyone. I would like to welcome the management and thank them for this 
opportunity. We have with us today Arnob Roy, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer; 
AVS Prasad, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Kumar N. Sivarajan, Chief Technology Officer; 
Preetham Uthaiah, Chief Operating Officer; and Sanjay Malik, Chief Strategy and Business 
Officer.

Arnob Roy: 
Thank you. Good evening, and welcome to the Tejas Networks Earnings Call of Q2. I'd like to 
start with a summary of the quarter. We ended with a revenue of INR406 crores as opposed to 
INR262 crores on a year-on-year basis. The profit after tax was a loss of INR207 crores, which 
was an improvement from minus INR307 crores of Q2 of FY26. And order book at the end of the 
quarter was INR2,315 crores while Q1 order book was INR1,529 crores. From a revenue mix, 
India was 88% compared to the international revenues of 12%. And from an order book mix, 96% 
of India and 4% of international. And the key reason was because of our order book being -- it was 
a receipt of the LOI and subsequent POs for 18,000-plus 4G sites for the BSNL 4G network 
expansion. And that's the reason why the India component of the order book went up substantially. 
 
The Q2 revenues were driven by shipments of optical IP and FTTx products to our private 
operators and system integrators. And we also started the initial shipments of the BSNL 
expansion order. We also did initial shipments of our end-to-end 5G solution to international 
customer in South America. This is a business that we had won last quarter, and we started our 
shipments in this quarter. We filed 26 patents in Q2, taking our global patent count to 748. 
 
I'll now hand it over to our CFO to take us through the numbers. 
AVS Prasad: 
Good evening, everyone. The Q2 FY27 revenue from operations is around INR406 crores 
compared to Q2 of INR262 crores in FY26, an increase of around 55%. The improved scale reflects 
the continued recovery in terms of business performance. And at H1 levels compared to INR464 
crores in H1 FY26, we are at INR808 crores. This represents approximately around 74% year-on-
year growth. 
 
At the EBITDA level, compared to INR293 crores negative in Q2 of FY26, we are at INR108 
crores negative in the current quarter. And at the PAT level compared to INR307 crores negative 
in Q2 FY26, we are at negative INR207 crores in Q2 FY27.

In terms of the balance sheet items, the net working capital compared to Q1 FY27 is lower at

nonrecourse bill discounting which also has customer advance settlements, which happens on a

INR4,384 crores in Q2 FY27. This increase is on account of continued investments in terms of 
capex at Tejas as per the plan and also in terms of funding operational costs.

mobile network. We did the initial RAN shipments and also shipped and deployed our 5G core in

in custom bands as a combination of custom bands and also high-power radios in custom bands. 
So this is one of the interesting new engagements that has happened based on our radio technology

received an LOI from a new SI partner to supply IP/MPLS routers for upgrading the BharatNet 
middle mile network in 3 states. We also won a significant order for building a strategic OTN 
network -- it's a pan-India network for a Government of India Enterprise. And we have received 
the orders subsequently for the shipment. 
 
We also received POs to supply our GPON FTTx products for high-speed broadband access 
networks from several leading ISPs in India. They are our existing customers who have increased 
their deployment of broadband connectivity to their customers. We also won a new Tier 1 pan-
African telecom operator network and we were selected for optical equipment, our 400-gig 
optical equipment for this network. This is, again, a new customer footprint that we have won in 
that continent.

our patents, as I mentioned, taking it to 748, out of which 266 are 5G Advanced and 6G

membership of TSDSI's Governing Council, which defines the standards applicable for India.

demonstrated a real-world application of 6G by showing 6G sensing technology for drone and 
vehicle detection, and this was done in partnership with Qualcomm.

radio baseband to core, the WavePlex family of products. We showed our hyperscale network 
solutions for cloud and AI data centers. And we also showed our future-ready optical access 
transport and routing portfolio scaled for the AI era. 
 
During the conference, we participated in several thought leadership and other discussions, we 
had participated in 4 speaking sessions on 6G foundations and road map at the Bharat 6G 
Symposium. We also participated in the CEO and CTO roundtables with Honorable Ministry of 
Communications. And we have several panelists in the IMC business and technology sessions.

5G deployment in emerging markets and the 5G rollouts, which are supposed to continue until 
2030. And we continue to get new engagements for POCs and many of them leading to a 
commercial discussion stage with operators in these emerging markets. 
 
The other important factor is the global 5G FWA subscriptions, the fixed wireless access are 
supposed to triple and reach close to 90 million by 2030. The expansion of existing 4G network 
domestically, and that's part of the BSNL 4G network expansion that's happening and AI driving 
the acceleration of 6G commercialization and which will drive the need for higher capacity 
massive MIMO radios and AI-native baseband and core. 
 
Similarly, in wireline, the drivers are the AI data centers driving generational upgrades of access 
aggregation and metro backbone networks, high-speed growth and expansion of high-speed 
enterprise connectivity, increase in residential broadband connectivity and as the wireless 
networks expand, the build-out of the backhaul connectivity for the expanded mobile 5G 
networks. 
 
And there's a continued modernization of utility networks that's happening and which we 
continue to win as we transition the networks from the older TDM networks to a modern packet-

which will support up to 5 frequency bands in 1 site. So that's essentially for one site, a very

consumption, for predicting the mobility of users, all of these, we are moving to AI-based so the 
performance is better. 
 
In IMC 2026, last week, we showed integrated sensing and communications. So essentially, we 
are showing that the 5G radios that we deploy can be used like a radar. So they can sense and 
detect traffic, drones, cars, moving cars, floods, and so on. So that's a demonstration that was 
well received last week at IMC. 
 
Last year, we had shown Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces, which is a technology that 
improves fixed wireless access in 5G. The wireline portfolio, we won the MAN tender and 
deployed it in the last 2 years, which is based on IP/MPLS. And we are now expanding our 
IP/MPLS for routing portfolio to cover higher bit rates so that we can address much bigger 
networks. 
 
In the access, latency, low latency is becoming important, especially because of AI-based 
applications. And we are developing high-capacity, low-latency access platforms at 200 gig and 
beyond. In terms of the backbone, there's both packet-based and optical-based backbone at 
terabits per second speeds, and we are investing in these products as well. 
 
Lastly, we already are rolling out AI-based network management solutions. We call it the Tejas 
Observability Platform, TOP. And this helps our customers, our telco customers optimize their 
network, predict equipment faults and reroute or recover from network faults through resilience 
and also to plan the capacity because we can predict when the traffic will grow and their capacity 
will start to run out. This is already being deployed by many of our customers today.
